walkthrough: Goal: put the ink on one layer and keep it apart from what is drawn on another, hide a layer to look at the rest, fade one, change which lies on top, throw one away, and find it all again after closing the app.

Entry: open OpenPaint on the tablet (2880 x 1800, landscape) on an empty library. The side bar at the left edge holds the grey undo and redo arrows; at the top bar's right end sits the Layers button, a small stack of sheets. Draw a black curve with the pen: it lands on Layer 1.

Tap the Layers button: a panel drops down under it at the right edge, over the canvas. Its header reads Layers with a plus at the right; one row, Layer 1, highlighted as the layer being drawn on, an open eye at its right end; below the rows the active layer's Opacity slider at 100 % and the move up, move down and delete buttons (move up, move down and delete are grey: there is only one layer).

Tap the plus: Layer 2 appears above Layer 1 and becomes the highlighted one. Tap the canvas outside the panel with a finger: the panel closes and nothing is drawn. Draw a second curve with the pen across the first: it lies on top, on Layer 2.

Open the panel again and tap the eye of Layer 2: it closes and the second curve disappears from the canvas; tap it again and the curve is back. Drag the Opacity slider of Layer 2 to the left, to about a third: the second curve fades while the finger moves; lifting it is one step for undo.

Select Layer 1 by tapping its name and tap move up: Layer 1 is now listed above Layer 2 (the canvas looks the same: while the only ink is black, black over faded black is black in either order; colours arrive in S12). Tap undo in the side bar: the order is back. Tap redo: Layer 1 on top again.
Tap delete: Layer 1 and its curve are gone, Layer 2 is highlighted. There is no confirmation: tap undo and Layer 1 is back with its curve, highlighted again.
A pen stroke that starts on the panel never paints. With the panel open, a pen stroke on the canvas outside it closes the panel and draws, on the highlighted layer.

Leave the app and let the system close it, open it again: the same layers in the same order, the same visibility and opacity, the same highlighted layer, pixel for pixel. Undo is grey: history is not stored. The panel is closed.

Failure: a button that cannot act now is grey and ignores taps (move up on the top layer, move down on the bottom one, delete with one layer left, plus at 256 layers). Not here: renaming, thumbnails, dragging rows to reorder, blend modes, groups.
